label: MLE of mean vector and covariance — unseen mastery test

items.stem: For iid Nₚ(μ,Σ), the MLE of μ is:
items.explanation: The normal likelihood is maximised over μ at the coordinate-wise sample mean vector.

items.stem: The denominator in the covariance MLE with unknown mean is:
items.explanation: The maximum likelihood covariance averages centred outer products over all n observations.

items.stem: If d is p×1, dd′ has dimension:
items.explanation: Multiplying a p×1 column by its 1×p transpose produces a p×p matrix.

items.stem: The unbiased sample covariance uses denominator:
items.explanation: Estimating the mean consumes one degree of freedom, giving n−1 for unbiased covariance.

items.stem: If n=5, the multiplier converting unbiased S to covariance MLE is:
items.explanation: The relationship is Σ̂=((n−1)/n)S, giving 4/5.

items.stem: The covariance matrix in a nonsingular multivariate normal model is:
items.explanation: A nonsingular multivariate normal covariance parameter is symmetric positive definite.

items.stem: For observations (1,2)′, (3,4)′, (5,6)′, the sample mean is:
items.explanation: Coordinate-wise averages are three and four.

items.stem: The centred sum is [[8,4],[4,2]] from n=4. The MLE (1,1) entry is:
items.explanation: Divide the centred sum by n=4; the top-left entry is 8/4=2.

items.stem: Which is the multivariate normal covariance MLE?
items.explanation: The MLE uses centred observations and divides the outer-product sum by n.

items.stem: If n=10, the MLE covariance equals what fraction of unbiased covariance?
items.explanation: The ratio is (n−1)/n, which equals 9/10.

items.stem: For n=3 and centred sum [[6,3],[3,2]], the MLE (2,2) entry is:
items.explanation: The lower-right entry is two; divide by n=3 to obtain two-thirds.

items.stem: Which statements are correct?
items.explanation: The first three statements describe the MLE and unbiased estimator correctly; the covariance MLE is biased downward.
statements: The mean vector MLE is x̄.
The covariance MLE divides the centred outer-product sum by n.
The unbiased covariance divides the same sum by n−1.
The covariance MLE is unbiased for Σ in every finite sample.

A.why: The multivariate normal likelihood is maximised at the sample mean vector.

B.why: The Gaussian covariance MLE uses divisor n.

C.why: The n−1 divisor gives the unbiased sample covariance.

D.why: The covariance MLE is biased downward; scaling by n/(n−1) gives the unbiased estimator.

items.stem: The covariance MLE is symmetric because:
items.explanation: Each dd′ is symmetric, and sums and scalar multiples preserve symmetry.

items.stem: For p variables and n observations, centred covariance rank is at most:
items.explanation: Centred deviations sum to zero, so their span has dimension at most n−1 and p.

items.stem: For n=6 and S=[[3,1],[1,2]], the MLE (1,1) entry is:
items.explanation: Multiply S by 5/6; the top-left entry is 3×5/6=2.5.

items.stem: When μ is unknown, deviations in the covariance MLE are taken from:
items.explanation: The likelihood gives μ̂=x̄, so covariance is centred at the sample mean.

items.stem: For June 2026 Q37 observations (1,2)′, (4,4)′, (4,3)′, the covariance MLE is:
items.explanation: The centred outer-product sum is [[6,3],[3,2]]. Divide by n=3 to obtain [[2,1],[1,2/3]], official option D.

items.stem: Which statements about the covariance MLE are correct?
items.explanation: The MLE is symmetric and semidefinite; its rank is bounded by min(p,n−1), but positive definiteness is not guaranteed.
statements: It must be positive definite for every sample.

A.why: A sum of symmetric outer products remains symmetric.

B.why: For every a, a′Σ̂a is a sum of squared projections divided by n.

C.why: If n≤p or observations lie in a lower-dimensional subspace, the sample covariance is singular.

D.why: Centred deviations span at most n−1 dimensions and no more than p.

items.stem: If n=8, the ratio of MLE covariance to unbiased covariance is:
items.explanation: The MLE covariance is ((n−1)/n)S, giving 7/8 for n=8.

items.stem: For the June 2026 Q37 centred sum [[6,3],[3,2]], which statements are correct?
items.explanation: The MLE divides by three; unbiased covariance divides by two. The off-diagonal entries remain symmetric.
statements: The MLE covariance uses divisor n−1.

B.why: Divide the centred sum by three.

C.why: The unbiased covariance divides by two, giving [[3,3/2],[3/2,1]].

D.why: The maximum likelihood estimator divides by n, not n−1.
